design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (deficiency_balance_resolution, env_0072). Relaunch round 1: carried on from the predecessor's plan.md and task_tools.py; the design below was revised against XF_recipe.md (factor independence, assembly order, shape test, no tier selecting a rate base) before any seed was written.

1. Why this is a good test. Renata Szabo asks only for a new monthly payment plan on her leftover deficiency balance. The plan installment policy states that, after a broken arrangement in the rolling 12 months, "When the account had a broken arrangement in the rolling 12 months, the monthly installment of a new plan is fixed only after the account's ledger carries the restart down payment, posted after the latest broken date as a payment that carries no arrangement." The agent must notice the broken plan f4cf6a5e-09ab-4901-a81b-75e1e8e6491b (broken_date 2026-08-12) in the offers, see on the ledger that no payment carrying no arrangement was posted after it, find in the restart down payment policy that this payment is the restart down payment and how it is figured (five schedules over the account's offers and ledger, the recovery case and the contract ledger), hand the payment to the borrower (her own write), and only then figure the plan installment (six schedules) on the reduced balance. Difficulty comes from reading the policy, reconciling ledgers across three products and ordering the writes; there is one tool per action and no near-synonym tools.

2. Scope snapshot. Claimed by task 0: deficiency_ext_restart_down_payment (tool pay_restart_down_payment_04892a83, owner user) and deficiency_ext_plan_installment (tool record_payment_plan_offer_3f4fb3a9, owner agent). Reserved for task 1 (draw 2 prerequisites): deficiency_ext_lump_sum_settlement, deficiency_ext_installment_settlement, deficiency_ext_settlement_installment with their three tools — the settlement side of the charter (lump-sum offer, installment-settlement acceptance, settlement start), disjoint from the plan side claimed here. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts [5, 6]; R takes 5 factors, P takes 6.

3. Factor card — restart down payment (result 333.96):
- hardship_relief [parameter]: evidence offer 52b0fb8c-9ccb-44b0-bd9c-95edab5a4877 offer_date 2025-11-05 hardship_document medical_disability_statement (11 whole months before today); tier lasting hardship document within the look-back; value 3.0 points; baseline gives 500.24 (gold 333.96).
- surrender_relief [parameter, cross-difficulty recovery]: evidence recovery case 4178ae4a-8b13-44f9-9db2-cce6ee1548ae recovery_method voluntary_surrender, keys_obtained true; tier voluntary surrender with the key; value 2.0 points; baseline gives 444.82 (gold 333.96).
- broken_run_relief [parameter]: evidence plan f4cf6a5e-09ab-4901-a81b-75e1e8e6491b accepted_at 2025-12-03 11:26:54 CST, broken_date 2026-08-12 -> 8 whole months; tier at least run_mid_months (4) but fewer than run_long_months (9); value 1.0 point; baseline gives 389.39 (gold 333.96).
- contract_history_relief [parameter, cross-difficulty contract]: evidence contract 3d18332a-d062-4242-b805-c454234e948a: 23 contract_payment_posted rows of payment_type installment, 0 returned; the sale_proceeds payment 3f25fe4e-0c14-4d0b-a8de-5b2573739c2b is not counted; tier at least 12 but fewer than 24; value 0.5 point; baseline gives 361.68 (gold 333.96).
- make_good_addition [method]: evidence returned payment acd6afad-f8f7-4c8d-95c1-45033db74840 dated 2026-08-01 amount 139.97; tier returned payments within the look-back; method: add their total 139.97 after rounding; baseline gives 193.99 (gold 333.96).
- whole baseline (computation document only): 554.27.
Factor card — plan installment (result 121.54, evaluated after the restart down payment):
- installment_basis_method [method]: evidence offer 52b0fb8c-9ccb-44b0-bd9c-95edab5a4877 carries medical_disability_statement within 12 whole months; tier a hardship document within the look-back; method: basis = balance / 48 = 109.288958; baseline gives 145.85 (gold 121.54).
- rebreak_surcharge [parameter]: evidence latest broken_date 2026-08-12, 2 whole months before today; tier fewer than rebreak_recent_months (6); value +10.0%; baseline gives 110.69 (gold 121.54).
- returned_surcharge [parameter]: evidence 1 returned payment within 12 whole months (2026-08-01); tier exactly one; value +4.0%; baseline gives 117.20 (gold 121.54).
- paydown_reduction [parameter]: evidence posted 1,653.72 less returned 139.97 = 1,513.75 over original 6,722.47 = 0.2252; tier at least 0.20 but below 0.40; value -3.0%; baseline gives 124.80 (gold 121.54).
- credit_tier_surcharge [parameter, cross-difficulty contract]: evidence contract 3d18332a-d062-4242-b805-c454234e948a variant_name Tier 6 Fresh Start; tier Tier 6 Fresh Start; value +5.0%; baseline gives 116.12 (gold 121.54).
- recent_payer_reduction [parameter]: evidence 4 = posted rows dated 2026-04-28, 2026-05-28, 2026-06-28, 2026-07-28 and today's restart down payment, less the return of 2026-08-01; the 2026-03-28 installment is 6 whole months back and excluded; tier recent_many_count (2) or more; value -4.0%; baseline gives 125.88 (gold 121.54).
- whole baseline (computation document only): 130.22.
Near-misses: the contract's sale_proceeds payment 3f25fe4e-0c14-4d0b-a8de-5b2573739c2b would lift the restart contract payments from 23 to 24 (the next tier) if counted — the rule counts payment_type installment only; the 2026-03-28 plan installment is exactly 6 whole months back and is outside the plan recent payments; the latest broken arrangement is also 68 days old (inside recent_break_days 90), but the make-good takes the returned-payment tier first, so adding the broken installment instead is a misreading only when no return is in the window. No stamp names any tier: there is no hardship flag, no surrender-credit field, no tier flag; every tier is derived from offers, ledger rows, the recovery case and the contract ledger.
Method shape tables. make_good_addition: returned tier = SUM of returned amount_usd (input A); recent-break tier = LATEST installment_amount_usd of the broken offer (input B, different field); nothing tier = 0 while both other tiers are positive over their domain — every pair differs in inputs. installment_basis_method: hardship tier = balance / plan_max_term_months (one tariff input); carry tier = max(standard, broken installment) (adds an input and a max pick); standard = max(min dollars, pct of balance, balance / term) (three-way max) — each pair differs by an input or an operation.
Independence: every factor's bindings read only records, parameters and the plain bindings dp_balance / dp_broken_date (R) and pi_balance / pi_standard / pi_term_floor (P); no factor binding reads another factor's binding; assembly lives only in dp_pct/result and pi_adjust_pct/pi_adjusted/result and is stated once (R: points summed, subtracted, percent applied, rounded half up, make-good added after; P: percents summed, applied once to the basis, floors, round up at the end).

4. Base-invariant card. Exact write subject of both writes: deficiency_payment_posted (governing: deficiency_evt_payments, deficiency_agg_separate_resolution). posting_account_status: "Payments and credits are posted only to an account whose status is open, on_payment_plan or on_settlement_plan; a referred account is serviced only by the agency (agency_accounts_serviced_by_agency) and a closed account takes no further postings." — initial_state.deficiency_accounts.5879778a-a555-4096-aae5-578d1eb51f06.status = open (positive case); a referred or closed status would refuse (negative case, not this world). deficiency_agg_separate_resolution: one account named, nothing combined. Lineage refs also carried: deficiency_payment_plan (restart and installment clauses, overwritten as declared; the max_broken_arrangements_12m bar stays: 1 broken arrangement < 2), deficiency_opening (the post-sale explanation was mailed 2025-08-25, activity 027479a0-1726-4046-944f-c3f73824bc24, before every demand or offer; no dispute; Texas 4-year limitations not reached), deficiency_closure_and_referral (last unreturned payment 2026-06-28, 113 days before today, below the 120-day referral clock, so the account is open and not referred). No time-kind eligibility applies to deficiency_payment_posted, so temporal_feasibility is empty; the plan offer validity (14 days) starts with this offer and is not a gate on recording it.
Overwrites: R retires "Where the account had a broken arrangement ... a down payment of plan_restart_down_payment_pct of the balance" and replaces it with its own scoped sentence (same scope: accounts with a broken arrangement; accounts without one need none); P retires "The monthly installment is the greater of ... on the acceptance date, rounded up to the cent" for offers on balances of at least min_balance_for_plan_usd and restates that small balances keep the small-balance terms and the installment count and due dates stay as stated.

5. Business-object card. Target: Deficiency Balance Account 5879778a-a555-4096-aae5-578d1eb51f06 (Band 3, opened 2025-08-20, original 6,722.47), the only deficiency account of customer 5a10de2f-87eb-42bf-997b-5ab6b7a26422; produced by contract 3d18332a-d062-4242-b805-c454234e948a (Tier 6 Fresh Start, liquidated) and recovery case 4178ae4a-8b13-44f9-9db2-cce6ee1548ae (voluntary_surrender, sold 2025-08-20). Rows read: 2 offers (52b0fb8c-9ccb-44b0-bd9c-95edab5a4877 expired hardship lump sum; f4cf6a5e-09ab-4901-a81b-75e1e8e6491b broken plan), 10 deficiency ledger rows, 8 recovery activities, 27 contract ledger rows. The returned row acd6afad-f8f7-4c8d-95c1-45033db74840 returns the 2026-07-28 installment; it is included in the make-good and returned counts and offsets that installment in the paydown share. Writes: one payment row (no arrangement) on 5879778a-a555-4096-aae5-578d1eb51f06; one offer row on 5879778a-a555-4096-aae5-578d1eb51f06.

6. Seed rows. Contract seeded from origination: 23 autopay installments of 470.43 (simple interest, actual/365, interest first), the late charge of 7.06 on the 2025-06-15 installment (5% of 470.43 reduced once by 20% autopay and 50% first-delinquency relief) (the 2025-07-15 installment's charge date fell after the 2025-07-23 repossession, so none), the sale-proceeds payment of 2,920.00 applied interest 667.10 -> three installments due -> fee -> additional principal, the fee settlement, and the balance transfer of 6,722.47. Recovery case seeded from the surrender request (2025-07-21): fees from the Class 1 schedule (surrender fee 120.00 = class fee 150.00 less the 30.00 prompt-surrender credit, transport 125.00, reconditioning 240.00 with invoice, storage 26 days x 25.00 = 650.00 posted at sale, auction 295.00), the notice of intent to sell (2025-07-24, earliest sale 2025-08-08, reinstatement amount 1,192.92), the expense settlement from proceeds (1,430.00), and the post-sale explanation. The selling dealer's agreement is outside this task's world: no rule read here turns on it, so the contract's dealer link is left empty in the seed rather than pointing at an unread row. Historical offers are priced by this charter's own policies on the world of their day. No automatic clause fires: the account is open with no plan (no grace clock), 113 days without an unreturned payment (< 120), broken arrangements 1 (< 2).

7. Persona. A tired, organised receptionist; volunteers only the goal (a new monthly plan offer, no acceptance today), the natural situation (car given back, plan cancelled after a bounce) and an approximate balance; gives phone, SSN last four and ZIP when asked (date of birth and email only if one more is requested); a health/work answer only if asked; the payment only as a passive reaction once the agent explains that a payment must come first and hands it over; closes when told the offer is recorded with its monthly amount. She never names a down payment or a prior step.

8. Problem-tree card. Root deficiency_ext_plan_installment; prerequisite deficiency_ext_restart_down_payment. Edge kind value_input, gate pi_balance, form state, sentence "When the account had a broken arrangement in the rolling 12 months, the monthly installment of a new plan is fixed only after the account's ledger carries the restart down payment, posted after the latest broken date as a payment that carries no arrangement." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; the waited-on side is a record-visible state (a payment carrying no arrangement on the ledger, posted after the latest broken date); no tool, id or code token; strength "only after", scope limited to accounts with a broken arrangement in 12 months, matching the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty posts a payment carrying no arrangement (pay_restart_down_payment_04892a83); the restart policy names that payment "the restart down payment" and says it is collected as a payment carrying no arrangement, so sentence + ledger + restart rule lead to that write. Opening state false: broken plan f4cf6a5e-09ab-4901-a81b-75e1e8e6491b (2026-08-12) and no later payment without arrangement (evidence in prerequisite_closure). Resolver owner: user (the borrower authorises her own payment). Deletion sensitivity: skipping it gives 132.80 instead of 121.54. Topological order R -> P; no parallel edges. The tools validate nothing (see tools_do_not_block).

9. Standard solution. Locate (phone) -> verify (phone, 4417, 77083) -> read the account, offers, ledger, recovery case and activities, contract and contract ledger -> figure the restart down payment 5,542.68 x 3.5% = 193.99 + returned 139.97 = 333.96 -> unlock and hand over pay_restart_down_payment_04892a83; the borrower pays 333.96 (balance 5,208.72) -> figure the installment on 5,208.72: basis 108.515 x 1.12 = 121.5368 -> 121.54 -> unlock and call record_payment_plan_offer_3f4fb3a9.
Careless errors a careful agent avoids: figuring the plan on 5,542.68 before the payment (132.80); paying the plain 10% (554.27); counting the sale-proceeds payment as an installment (restart percent 3.0 instead of 3.5); adding the broken installment instead of the returned total; counting the 2026-03-28 installment as recent; using the standard 2.5% basis though a hardship document is on file (145.85).

10. Verification (executed). A scratch builder (removed at the end of the run under the coordinator's rule) evaluated each policy with check_compute's own build_env on initial_state and on the world after the real tool writes (erlbench DB + ToolContext); check_compute.py --task 0 recomputes the same figures at handling time and re-runs every substitution below: R = 333.96, P = 121.54, P with R skipped = 132.80; factor substitutions R {hardship_relief: 500.24, surrender_relief: 444.82, broken_run_relief: 389.39, contract_history_relief: 361.68, make_good_addition: 193.99, baseline: 554.27}; P {installment_basis_method: 145.85, rebreak_surcharge: 110.69, returned_surcharge: 117.20, paydown_reduction: 124.80, credit_tier_surcharge: 116.12, recent_payer_reduction: 125.88, baseline: 130.22}. Gate outputs are recorded in worklog.md.

11. Closure. policy -> tool -> computation -> call -> terminal state: deficiency_ext_restart_down_payment -> pay_restart_down_payment_04892a83 -> computations[0] (step 10, amount_usd 333.96) -> payment row + balance 5,208.72; deficiency_ext_plan_installment -> record_payment_plan_offer_3f4fb3a9 -> computations[1] (step 12, installment_amount_usd 121.54) -> offer row (payment_plan, offered, 5,208.72, 43 installments). required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies = [deficiency_ext_restart_down_payment, deficiency_ext_plan_installment].
solvability_contract: both writes carry posting_account_status (status open, account id bound to deficiency_account_id) and the separate-resolution scope; the payment's intent rests on the borrower's own line agreeing to pay herself, the offer's on her request for a monthly plan.
Draft recomputation from visible context: with the published rules, the ledger reads and the persona only, the hop "new plan after a broken arrangement waits on the restart down payment" is read from the plan policy's sentence; the restart figure and the installment are recomputed as in section 9 and agree with gold.
Rule <-> compute sweep: every binding of both policies quotes its rule sentence verbatim in compute_basis (the generator copies the sentence text); reverse sweep — each ladder sentence (hardship, surrender, run, contract history, make-good; basis, rebreak, returned, paydown, credit tier, recent payer) is implemented by its factor bindings, the assembly sentence by dp_pct/result and pi_adjust_pct/pi_adjusted/result, the latest-broken sentence by dp_broken_date. Decoy and absent-record probes: see section 12 (re-run in round 6).

12. Revision round 2. Round 2 (policy audit revision_1): every whole-month count in the charter now states its own counting rule inline — "whole months counted as the difference in calendar months, less one when the later date's day of the month is below the earlier date's" — which is exactly what MONTHS() does, so month-end starts (the 29th-31st) have one reading; and every policy that reads the latest broken arrangement states that no two arrangements of an account break on the same day. Plan recent-payer reduction now reads "any smaller count (none, or fewer once returns are taken off)" so a negative net count has a tier. No figure of this task moved (re-evaluated: 333.96 restart, 121.54 plan; every factor substitution unchanged). Adversarial probe sweep over every read and edge of the two policies (re-run in round 6 on the re-priced world; outcomes match the rule words): restart_down_payment: hardship doc on a declined offer dated today -> dp_hardship_pts=3.0; restart_down_payment: hardship offer exactly 12 whole months back -> dp_hardship_pts=0; restart_down_payment: month-end: hardship offer 2025-10-31, today 2026-10-30 -> dp_hardship_pts=3.0; restart_down_payment: voluntary surrender, keys false -> dp_surrender_pts=1.0; restart_down_payment: absent recovery case -> dp_surrender_pts=0; restart_down_payment: older broken arrangement present -> dp_broken_date=2026-08-12, dp_run_months=8; restart_down_payment: month-end run: accepted 2026-01-31, broken 2026-04-30 -> dp_run_months=2, dp_run_pts=0; restart_down_payment: returned contract installment -> dp_contract_paid=22, dp_history_pts=0.5; restart_down_payment: absent contract ledger -> dp_contract_paid=0, dp_history_pts=0; restart_down_payment: second return dated today -> dp_returned_total=279.94, dp_make_good=279.94; restart_down_payment: no return in window, break exactly 90 days back -> dp_days_since_break=90, dp_make_good=139.97; restart_down_payment: no return in window, break 91 days back -> dp_days_since_break=91, dp_make_good=0; plan_installment: no hardship doc: carry tier -> pi_basis=139.97, result=156.77; plan_installment: broken settlement (not a plan) is the latest break -> pi_since_break=1, pi_plan_broken=2026-08-12, pi_basis=139.97; plan_installment: net recent count pushed to zero by returns -> pi_recent_count=0, pi_recent_pct=0; plan_installment: credit counts toward paydown; waiver row does not -> pi_paid_down=1613.75; plan_installment: absent contract -> pi_tier_pct=0; plan_installment: no broken arrangement in 12 months -> pi_adjust_pct=2.0, result=110.69.

13. Revision round 6 (KB audit src items). Cross-product seed rows were re-priced by the published contract and recovery documents as of each row's own date: in task 0 the voluntary surrender fee is the class fee 150.00 less the 30.00 prompt-surrender credit (vehicle in 2 days after the case opened; Texas has no surrender-fee limit; book value 10,000.00 or more gives no value reduction; not a company drop-off lot) = 120.00; each contract late charge is 5% of the scheduled installment reduced once by 20% autopay relief (11 autopay drafts in the rolling 12 months) and 50% first-delinquency relief (no late charge in the rolling 12 months); in task 1 a second late charge on a later installment cannot be booked while the oldest unpaid installment already carries one. The notice of intent to sell states the reinstatement amount due on its own mailing date, the sale proceeds waterfall, the balance transfer, the post-sale explanation and the account's original deficiency follow. The lump-sum rule now records the hardship document the borrower hands in with the request for an offer, and its reduction reads only offers already recorded, so a first document goes on file with its offer and counts toward later figures; the earlier lump-sum offers were re-priced on that basis (no reduction on the offer that first carried the document). Every deficiency figure, historical offer, payment and gold value was rebuilt from those rows in date order; all tiers taken are unchanged, every factor still moves its result, and every baseline still differs from gold. Task 0 now: restart down payment 333.96, plan installment 121.54 (opening-world contrast 132.80).
user_scenario: You are Renata Szabo, 42, a dental office receptionist in Houston who sounds tired but organised; you keep your paperwork in a folder, apologise once for the mess, and then get to the point. Last summer you gave your 2017 Nissan Altima back to Harborline because you could not keep up with the payments, and after it was sold you were left owing a balance. You had been paying that leftover balance on a monthly plan until a payment bounced this summer and the plan was cancelled. You are calling today because you want to get back on a monthly payment plan for the leftover balance, and you want the representative to set the new plan offer up on this call; you will decide whether to accept it after reading its terms at home, so you do not accept or sign anything today. You do not know the exact balance: you think it is somewhere around fifty-five hundred dollars, and when the representative tells you a figure you take theirs. When asked to identify yourself you give your phone number, 7135550163, the last four digits of your Social Security number, 4417, and your ZIP code, 77083; only if one more detail is requested do you give your date of birth, 1984-03-22, or your email, renata.szabo@outlook.com. If the representative asks about your health or your work, you say your medical situation is the same as when you sent in your doctor's disability statement last fall and that you are working reduced hours. If the representative explains that a payment has to be made before the new plan can be offered, you agree without arguing and say you want to make it yourself from your checking account through the self-service payment; once the representative hands that payment over to you, you make it for exactly the amount they tell you and read back the new balance shown on your receipt. You never bring up a payment on your own. When the representative tells you the new plan offer has been recorded and gives you its monthly amount, you thank them, say you will look the terms over at home, and end the call.
